column1: # Known malicious or high-confidence suspicious VS Code / OpenVSX extension IDs.
# This canonical, conservative ID-level blocklist combines 322 publicly reported
# GlassWorm-linked entries, one incident-local review entry, and 95 separately
# attributed malicious entries. Campaign/source fields preserve each distinction;
# evil-twin and roblox-dropper labels do not mean GlassWorm.
# A listed ID does not mean every version in every registry was malicious. The
# audit intentionally matches all installed versions so removed releases and
#   Socket campaign feed and sleeper research:
#   Separately attributed Apee and heyheyhey campaigns:
# Socket CSV fetched 2026-08-18: 364 artifacts / 229 unique IDs;
# Secondary completeness cross-check: all 243 editor-extension IDs in
# Research cutoff: no later report found that explicitly attributed another
# extension wave to GlassWorm; similar post-June campaigns were kept separate.
# The sleeper-73 label is a report-family label: 73 initial IDs plus 22 later
# additions/activations (95 total), with confidence documented by Socket.
# The 95 non-GlassWorm IDs remain in this canonical file under evil-twin,
# evil-twin-apee, or roblox-dropper-heyheyhey campaign labels so one list gives
# complete scanner coverage without conflating threat attribution.
# Registry/version scope matters: the scanner deliberately blocks by ID, but
# same-ID releases in another registry or earlier/later versions can be clean.
# In particular, Socket implicated only Open VSX versions oorzc.ssh-tools@0.5.1,
# oorzc.scss-to-css-compile@1.3.4. Yeeth's Apee report lists malicious 0.0.x
# releases but explicitly excludes clean 0.0.3 decoys. The heyheyhey report
# implicates versions 4.7.0 for the five Ro* IDs and 4.6.9 for ManageBlox.
